**Aalborg Universitetshospital** is a major hospital located in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], Denmark [^src3]. It participates in the national clinical quality monitoring program for acute high-risk abdominal surgery, which is administered by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program (RKKP) [^src1]. The hospital's performance is systematically evaluated and benchmarked against national and regional standards using various clinical quality indicators to ensure transparency and support clinical quality development [^src3].

For the reporting period of September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023, Aalborg Universitetshospital's compliance with [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] (early antibiotic treatment within 3 hours) was recorded at 30.8% [^src1]. During this same period, the hospital's 30-day mortality rates were analyzed based on patient comorbidities. Specifically, there were 7 deaths within 30 days after acute surgery among 46 included patients with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]], representing a mortality rate of 15.2% (95% CI: 6.3-28.9) [^src3]. Additionally, demographic and cancer distribution data for the hospital's surgical patients were tracked, with 205 patients recorded in the supplementary age and gender analyses for that year [^src4].

In the subsequent reporting period from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024, the hospital's compliance with Indikator 1 was recorded at 34.6% [^src5]. Data from this period also shows that Aalborg Universitetshospital registered 8 deaths within 30 days after acute surgery among 32 included patients with a Charlson Score of 1 or 2, which is tracked under the supplementary indicator [[indikator-9b|Indikator 9b]] [^src9]. Furthermore, for patients with severe comorbidities (Charlson Score ≥ 3), the hospital registered 8 deaths within 30 days among 32 included patients, monitored under [[indikator-9c|Indikator 9c]] [^src9]. The demographic profile for this later period included 208 patients in the supplementary analyses [^src10]. Other supplementary mortality indicators for the 2023-2024 period showed a 15.3% rate on page 51 [^src7] and a 2.3% rate on page 61 [^src8].
